title: Creating Your First Workflow knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Creating Your First Workflow?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
A minimal workflow declares a name, trigger under `on`, job, runner through `runs-on`, and ordered steps that use actions or shell commands.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: A minimal workflow declares a name, trigger under `on`, job, runner through `runs-on`, and ordered steps that use actions or shell commands.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of creating your first workflow: A minimal workflow declares a name, trigger under `on`, job, runner through `runs-on`, and ordered steps that use actions or shell commands. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
questions.answer_key: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
questions.explanation: Creating a .yml or .yaml workflow file: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to creating your first workflow?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A minimal workflow declares a name, trigger under `on`, job, runner through `runs-on`, and ordered steps that use actions or shell commands. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
